_comment: SAMPLE REPORT with illustrative data for a fictional plumbing company. Not a real business.

sections.title: What your website does today
sections.lead: Right now, Google sends exampleplumbing.com about 6 visitors a month. The business is not in the Google Maps top 10 for “plumber near me” or “emergency plumber”, has 9 Google reviews, and is not mentioned by AI assistants. The site also has no privacy policy, terms or accessibility statement (see section 7). This is a sample report; all figures are illustrative.

sections.title: 1. Website traffic
sections.lead: Local independent plumbers get 45 to 420 visitors a month from Google. Example Plumbing gets about 6.

blocks.title: Example Plumbing gets about 6 Google visitors a month
blocks.subtitle: Estimated monthly visitors from Google search, local independent plumbers
blocks.note: At the current $1,200/month marketing spend, that is about $200 per visitor.
blocks.source: Source: Open SEO (DataForSEO) and Semrush US organic traffic estimates. Franchises such as Roto-Rooter and Mr. Rooter are left out because their figures cover many locations.

blocks.text: Advertisers in Bergen County pay $48 per click for “emergency plumber near me” and $62 for “water heater replacement”. One extra water heater or sewer line job a month covers the cost of fixing this.

blocks.title: Lead response test: no reply after 5+ minutes
paragraphs: We submitted the website’s “Request Service” form on a weekday afternoon. More than 5 minutes later, nobody had called, texted or emailed. A homeowner with a burst pipe calls the next plumber on Google.

Speed matters: the 2007 MIT/InsideSales Lead Response Management study (15,000+ leads) found that contacting a web lead within 5 minutes instead of 30 gave 100 times the odds of reaching them and 21 times the odds of qualifying them.

sections.title: 3. Google Maps and reviews
sections.lead: Most plumbing calls come from the Google Maps results. Example Plumbing shows up at #16 for “plumber near me” searched from Hackensack.

blocks.title: Competitors have 150–900 Google reviews. Example Plumbing has 9.

blocks.text: Source: Open SEO Google Maps data.
Your Google Business Profile needs work

items: Primary category is “Contractor” instead of “Plumber”; “Emergency plumber” is not added as a category.
Hours show 8am–5pm even though you offer 24/7 emergency service, so Google hides you for night searches.
Only 3 photos and no services listed (water heaters, drains, sewer, gas lines).

sections.title: 4. AI search visibility
sections.lead: When someone asks ChatGPT or Google's AI “who's a good emergency plumber in Hackensack?”, Example Plumbing is not mentioned.

blocks.text: Source: Semrush AI Search. AI assistants draw on Google profiles, reviews and directory listings, so fixing local presence also fixes AI visibility.
The site has 38 links from 21 websites, mostly low-quality directories, and an Authority Score of 4 out of 100.

items: Good links to build on: the local chamber of commerce and a plumbing-supply house that lists trusted contractors.
Missing trust signals: the NJ Master Plumber license number, proof of insurance and warranty terms are not on the site.
Conflicting details: the phone number on Yelp and Angi differs from the website and Google profile.

sections.title: 6. Website health check
sections.lead: The site has no critical errors, but every service is crammed onto one page and Google can't tell what you do best.

rows: 71 out of 100; main content appears after 3.6 seconds (target: under 2.5)
Heading order, long titles and descriptions

items: One “Services” page covers everything; there are no pages for water heaters, drains, sewer lines, gas lines or emergencies.
No reviews, before-and-after photos or team photos on the site.
The “24/7 emergency” message is only in the footer, not at the top of the page.

sections.title: 7. Legal and compliance risk
sections.lead: The site has no privacy policy, terms and conditions or accessibility statement, yet it collects names, phone numbers and addresses through its service form.

blocks.text: What it can cost: real examples

rows: Plaintiff firms scan small-business websites and send demand letters or file suit. About 3,100 federal website accessibility lawsuits were filed in 2025, and over 5,000 including state courts.
An Orlando flower shop paid $7,000+ in late 2024; its website was managed by a third party. Average out-of-court settlement: about $25,000–$30,000.
Only the U.S. Department of Justice can seek it. Rare for small businesses, but it is the legal maximum.
Up to $118,225 for a first violation and $236,451 for each later one.
Appointment or marketing texts sent without documented consent, under the federal TCPA.
$500 per text, up to $1,500 if willful, plus attorney's fees.
Carriers require a public privacy policy, terms and an SMS opt-in before approving business texting (A2P 10DLC).
No fine, but dispatch texts, review requests and AI follow-up cannot be switched on.

blocks.text: Not legal advice; have a licensed attorney review final policies. Sources: Seyfarth Shaw (adatitleiii.com, 2026); UsableNet 2025; WFTV/AOL (Leaf & Blossom, Co.); 28 CFR 36.504 (July 2025); Jimerson Firm (TCPA); Twilio A2P 10DLC docs; Verstian 2026 (settlement average).

sections.title: 8. What we recommend
sections.lead: The fastest gains come from Google Maps, reviews and answering every lead in under a minute.

phases.title: Days 1–30: foundation
items: Fix the Google Business Profile: “Plumber” and “Emergency plumber” categories, 24/7 hours, services, 20+ photos
Make the phone number identical on the website, Google, Yelp, Angi and BBB
Publish a privacy policy, terms and accessibility statement; add SMS consent and the license number
Start automatic review requests by text after every job

phases.title: Days 31–60: content and coverage
items: Add pages for emergency plumbing, water heaters (tank and tankless), drain cleaning, sewer lines, gas lines and sump pumps
Add town pages for Hackensack, Teaneck, Paramus, Fort Lee and River Edge
Connect Google Search Console and Analytics in accounts you own

phases.title: Days 61–90: authority and more calls
items: Earn local links (chamber, supply houses, home inspectors, realtors)
Reach 50+ Google reviews
24/7 AI call answering and instant text replies so no emergency call goes to voicemail
Re-run this report to measure the change
